syntax.rationale: FLAGGED, NOT INVENTED (coord ruling 2(b): flag a page that genuinely has no declaration grammar rather than dressing inline mentions up as one). This change adds no property, no API and no policy grammar: it is a TLS key-aggregation and enterprise-policy REMOVAL, so the only syntax-shaped artefact on the page is the runtime probe added to #impact (an `openssl s_client` invocation, whose flag form is the thing a reader actually types). That is a command, not a declaration, and the validator forces `syntax: documented` on an implementation-sufficient claim - this is exactly the case the forced-documented rule cannot express honestly, and it is flagged for that bead rather than papered over.

notes: Carried source disagreement, neither side adjudicated (all sources re-fetched 2026-10-06): the page calls the cited draft-ietf-tls-ecdhe-mlkem an IETF draft and tells middlebox operators to support X25519Kyber768Draft00 or X25519MLKEM768; the cited draft URL now redirects to RFC 10024, which defines X25519MLKEM768 and says the X25519Kyber768Draft00 registry entry is obsolete. The cited ChromeStatus record itself still links its spec_link to the older draft-tls-westerbaan-xyber768d00-02 (also fetched 2026-10-06), describing the earlier X25519Kyber768Draft00 group. The page says the PostQuantumKeyAgreementEnabled policy could be used between Chrome 124 and 146; the ChromeStatus summary says it would be available through Chrome 145 and removed in Chrome 147 (fetched 2026-10-06); neither side is adjudicated here. The intent-to-ship thread describes its existence at the Chrome 124 rollout, not independent confirmation of the 147 removal. The example is a real OpenSSL 3.5+ s_client group probe, not a Chrome-specific JS API; local OpenSSL 3.0.13 cannot run that probe, so no negotiated output is asserted. The citation edit wraps the page's already-named IETF draft in a link AND, under the in-unit prose ruling, now says "(now RFC 10024)" so the citation is no longer stale. IN-UNIT PROSE REPAIR (coord 22:30Z: a divergence found in a page already open in a B1 unit is fixed in that unit, not deferred to a bead): the page now carries the disclosure sentence, both sides stated and neither adjudicated, with its as-of date inside the sentence so it can be pinned; the case is pinned in the curated table in scripts/source-disagreement.test.mjs, and deleting the sentence was mutation-proved to fail that fixture. EXAMPLE INDEPENDENTLY PROBED by gendn-impl (the worker honestly reported it could not run it): this VM carries OpenSSL 3.0.13, whose s_client DOES support -groups and -servername and produces exactly the probed line - `-groups X25519` returned 'Server Temp Key: X25519, 253 bits' - so the command's shape, flags and grep target are verified. The page's group name cannot be exercised here: 3.0.13 answers `group 'X25519MLKEM768' cannot be set`, which is the expected too-old-OpenSSL failure rather than a wrong command, and matches the page's own 'OpenSSL 3.5+' note. So the mechanism is verified and the MLKEM group name remains unrun on this host - stated rather than implied.
